script.speaker: Marta
script.line: Before we vote, I want to put it bluntly: pivoting the whole division into subscriptions now would be reckless.

script.speaker: Dean
script.line: With respect, Marta, sitting on the fence for another quarter is the reckless move. Our margins are already bleeding.

script.speaker: Marta
script.line: They're thin, not bleeding. And you're glossing over the fact that we'd have to gut half the sales team to fund this.

script.speaker: Dean
script.line: We'd redeploy them, not gut them. Honestly, I think you're clinging to a model that's had its day.

script.speaker: Chair
script.line: Let's not make this personal. Dean, walk us through the numbers you've floated.

script.speaker: Dean
script.line: Sure. If we shift sixty percent of revenue to subscription within eighteen months, churn aside, we'd stabilize cash flow by year three.

script.speaker: Marta
script.line: That's a big if. You're banking on churn staying under ten percent, which, frankly, is optimistic given our track record.

script.speaker: Dean
script.line: I'd rather bet on an ambitious plan than watch us get outpaced by every competitor who's already made the leap.

script.speaker: Chair
script.line: Marta, what would you propose instead?

script.speaker: Marta
script.line: A phased pilot. Test the subscription model in one region before we bet the farm on it company-wide.

script.speaker: Dean
script.line: That could've worked two years ago. Now it just delays the inevitable and lets rivals lock in customers first.

script.speaker: Marta
script.line: Or it stops us from torching capital on something half-baked. I've seen this movie before, Dean.

script.speaker: Chair
script.line: Both points are fair. Let's table a compromise: a pilot in two markets, with a hard deadline for a full rollout decision.

script.speaker: Dean
script.line: I could live with that, provided the deadline isn't so far out that it becomes an excuse to stall again.

script.speaker: Marta
script.line: Six months, then. Enough time for real data, not enough to drag our feet.

script.speaker: Chair
script.line: Agreed. I'll circulate the revised proposal, and we'll reconvene once the pilot numbers are in.

script.speaker: Dean
script.line: Fine by me. I just don't want caution to be the thing that sinks us.

script.speaker: Marta
script.line: And I don't want ambition to be the thing that bankrupts us. Let's see what the data says.

script.speaker: Priya
script.line: Thanks, everyone, for logging on at short notice. I won't sugarcoat it: we're restructuring three departments.

script.speaker: Operator
script.line: Good morning, everyone. I'll now hand the call over to CFO Renee Alvarez for the quarterly update.

script.speaker: Renee
script.line: Thanks. Revenue came in at two hundred ten million, up eight percent year-on-year, though slightly under our own guidance.

script.line: Renee, can you unpack why you missed guidance when bookings looked strong through most of the quarter?

script.speaker: Renee
script.line: Fair question. A handful of enterprise deals slipped into next quarter due to procurement delays on the client side.

script.speaker: Investor 1
script.line: Slipped, or lost? Those aren't the same thing, and investors will read this differently depending on which it is.

script.speaker: Renee
script.line: Slipped. We have signed letters of intent on three of the four deals; they're just not closed yet.

script.speaker: Investor 2
script.line: What about margins? They compressed by roughly two points. Is that a one-off or something we should get used to?

script.speaker: Renee
script.line: Partly one-off, tied to onboarding costs for two large clients. But input costs are also creeping up, so I won't oversell a quick fix.

script.line: So we should model continued pressure into next quarter, realistically?

script.speaker: Renee
script.line: I'd model modest pressure, yes, easing in the second half as the onboarding costs roll off.

script.speaker: Investor 1

script.speaker: Renee
script.line: A bit of both, if I'm being candid. We tightened approvals given the guidance miss, and the market for senior engineers is tight regardless.

script.speaker: Investor 2

script.line: Appreciate the transparency, Renee, even if the numbers themselves are a bit underwhelming this quarter.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.line: Mr. Kessler, thanks for making time. I understand you're unhappy with the renewal terms we sent over.

script.speaker: Kessler
script.line: Unhappy is putting it mildly. A twelve percent increase feels like you're taking us for a ride, frankly.

script.line: I hear you, and I want to be upfront: some of that reflects rising infrastructure costs we've absorbed for two years without passing them on.

script.speaker: Kessler
script.line: That's your problem to manage, not ours to fund. We can get a comparable service elsewhere for less.

script.line: You could, though I'd flag that most competitors don't offer the same uptime guarantees or dedicated support you get with us.

script.speaker: Kessler
script.line: Guarantees are nice on paper, but they don't mean much when the increase itself is what's straining our budget.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.line: Understood. What if we phased the increase, six percent this year and the remainder next year, tied to a longer contract?

script.speaker: Kessler
script.line: How much longer are we talking? I'm not signing a three-year lock-in just to soften a price hike.

script.speaker: Sophie
script.line: Eighteen months, not three years. And we'd throw in the premium support tier at no extra cost for that period.

script.speaker: Kessler

lessons.title: Handling an Ethics Complaint with Care

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: Thanks for coming in, Aiden. I want to be direct: a complaint's been filed alleging you pressured a vendor into a kickback arrangement.

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: That's a serious accusation, and frankly it's not true. Whoever filed this is twisting a conversation completely out of context.

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: I'm not here to accuse you outright. I need to walk through the specifics and hear your side before anything's decided.

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: Fair enough. What exactly is the vendor claiming happened?

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: They allege you implied their contract renewal depended on routing a portion of the invoice to a third party you'd name.

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: I did mention a referral partner during that call, but it was a legitimate subcontracting suggestion, not a kickback.

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: Can you walk me through why you brought that up in a contract negotiation at all? It's an unusual thing to raise.

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: In hindsight, I can see how it might've come across wrong. I should've kept that conversation strictly separate.

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: That's a meaningful admission. Was there any financial benefit to you personally in that referral?

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: None whatsoever. I have no stake in that company, and I'll happily have that verified through my financial disclosures.

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: We will be verifying it, as part of standard process, not because I doubt you specifically.

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: I understand. I just don't want this to snowball into something it isn't based on a poorly worded suggestion.

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: I take that seriously. Regardless of intent, though, mixing personal referrals into vendor negotiations crosses a line we take seriously.

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: Agreed, and I'll own that lapse in judgment. What happens next in the process?

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: We'll interview the vendor again, review the call notes, and likely require a compliance refresher regardless of the outcome.

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: That's fair. I'd rather go through the refresher than have any ambiguity linger over this.

script.speaker: HR Lead
script.line: Appreciate the cooperation, Aiden. We'll follow up within two weeks once the review's complete.

script.speaker: Aiden
script.line: Understood. I'd rather this be handled thoroughly than swept under the rug either way.
